stories.headline: 30 missing a year after Chisoti flash flood
stories.title: 30 missing a year after Chisoti flash flood
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 25: Thirty people remain missing a year after a cloudburst-triggered flash flood swept through Chisoti village in Paddar-Gulabgarh tehsil of Kishtwar district. The disaster left 63 bodies recovered and 127 injured, according to an RTI reply from the Kishtwar district administration provided to Jammu-based activist Raman Kumar Sharma. Of the 30 missing, 27 are yatris and three are local residents. The yatris included people from Jammu and other districts of the Jammu division, Uttarakhand, and Delhi who had travelled to Chisoti for the Chandi Mata Machail Yatra. For their families, a year has brought no closure. “We are still waiting for closure,” said Pawan Kumar, whose father, Somnath, 50, ran a seasonal tea stall. “We haven’t got any relief yet,” he said. Somnath is among the three missing locals. The others are Tulsi Devi, 50, and priest Bodhraj, 79. Tulsi was selling food to pilgrims when the BhotNallah - a tributary of the mighty Chenab river - overflowed. “My wife was selling food to pilgrims when the floodwaters came crashing through the village,” said her husband, Masti Ram, 55. “We waited for months hoping her body would be found. We are yearning to find even a body part so that we can perform her last rituals.” Tulsi left behind her 23-year-old son, Mandeep Singh, who has a neurological disability. Bodhraj, a longtime priest at the Kali Mata temple, was leading prayers when the flood struck. “He was our caretaker, protector, and spiritual guide,” said his granddaughter, Priya, 20. “We only want to find him so we can cremate him with full honour. Otherwise, our souls will never rest.” SashastraSeemaBal Head Constable HussanDass of Jammu lost seven family members. Only his wife’s body was recovered. “I desperately tried to contact my family, but their phones were switched off,” Dass told media personnel. SDRF, NDRF, and SSB teams searched for more than a month but found no trace of the others. Sonu Kumar lost his wife, son, and daughter. “Initially, we held on to the agonising hope that they might still be found alive,” he said. “As the days passed, that hope slowly faded.” Kumar said death certificates were issued for his missing family members, but compensation had not been released. Chisoti, 15 km from Gulabgarh-Paddar and 85 km from Kishtwar, serves as the base camp for the Chandi Mata MachailYatra, which draws more than 2 lakh devotees annually. Hamori, surrounded by six Buddhist-dominated villages, is the last motorable point- 6 kms from Chisoti, with Machail another 6 km ahead. Yatris cross a bridge, travel 5 km by dirt road, and trek another 6 km to Machail. The yatra is also a key source of livelihood. Residents run food stalls and ferry yatris on motorcycles. On August 14, 2025, about 2500 yatris were in Chisoti when the flood struck at 12:38 pm and nearly 15,000 had set out for the yatra. The torrent tore through the village, destroying homes, shops, a langar, and a security outpost. Survivor Sawant Singh said the force of the Chenab and its tributaries made recovery difficult. “The Chenab and its tributaries are so ferocious that once they wash someone away, it becomes extremely difficult to recover the body,” he said. “You may find a body or its fragments in the first day or two. After that, the chances become very slim.” Locals said some fragmented remains were recovered, but many victims were never found. The administration sanctioned Rs. 2.52 crore in exgratia relief for families whose relatives’ bodies were recovered, according to the RTI reply. A year later, families of the 30 missing continue to wait for their loved ones’ remains and closure.

stories.headline: How long will J&K beg from Delhi: Farooq Abdullah
stories.title: How long will J&K beg from Delhi: Farooq Abdullah
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 25: National Conference (NC) President Farooq Abdullah on Tuesday gave a pointed response when asked whether the Jammu and Kashmir government would review the recently approved electricity tariff hike, saying the region could not seek greater political autonomy while continuing to depend on New Delhi for financial support. “Tell me this, how long will you be a slave? You have to stand on your feet sometimes. When will you stand?” Abdullah said when reporters asked him about a possible review of the power tariff increase. “How long will you (J&K) beg from Delhi?” he asked. Taking the question beyond the immediate tariff hike, Abdullah linked Jammu and Kashmir’s economic dependence on the Centre with the demand for restoration of Article 370. “You want Article 370, but you beg. Two things cannot be combined,” he said. Abdullah said that Jammu and Kashmir would need to strengthen its own economic footing if it wanted to retain its dignity. “If you want your respect, then first try to stand on your feet,” he said. His remarks come at a time when the power tariff increase has become a major political issue in J&K. The Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission has approved an average 6.83 percent increase in electricity tariffs for 2026-27, with the revised rates scheduled to come into force from September 1. The decision has drawn protests from opposition parties, while industry representatives have also raised concerns over the impact of higher electricity costs. Chief Minister Omar Abdullah defended the hike, describing it as a “compulsion” rather than a choice. He argued that the increase is relatively modest compared with previous tariff revisions and maintained that his government remains committed to providing 200 units of free electricity to eligible households. The tariff dispute has also assumed significance because electricity was a prominent issue during the 2024 J&K Assembly elections, with the NC campaigning on a promise of providing 200 units of free electricity to households. Abdullah’s comments therefore come against a backdrop of growing political pressure over the tariff decision, but rather than directly addressing whether the hike could be reviewed, he used the question to argue that J&K needs greater economic self-reliance. Later, Abdullah was asked about the reported rise in crimes against women. He attributed the problem to what he described as a growing distance from religious values. “This is because we are very far from the words of Allah,” Abdullah said. He said that the issue was not confined to Muslims, saying people across communities had moved away from religion. “We are Muslims by name, not Muslims by deeds,” Abdullah said.

stories.headline: Power distribution inefficiencies can't be passed on to consumers: JERC
stories.title: Power distribution inefficiencies can't be passed on to consumers: JERC
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 25: Even as the Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission (JERC) has approved an average 6.83 percent increase in electricity tariffs in Jammu and Kashmir, it has made it clear that inefficiencies in power distribution cannot be passed on to consumers and has directed Kashmir Power Distribution Corporation Limited (KPDCL) and Jammu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (JPDCL) to take concrete measures to reduce losses. The revised tariff, approved by JERC for 2026-27, will come into effect from September 1. The increase was approved after the commission examined the revenue requirements of the two distribution companies. Against this backdrop, the commission's observations on distribution losses assume significance. It has specifically classified distribution loss as a controllable parameter, meaning the two distribution companies are expected to take measures within their control to bring such losses down instead of treating higher losses as a cost to be recovered from consumers. “The actual losses cannot be considered and inefficiencies cannot be passed on to the consumers,” the commission said. JERC said that KPDCL and JPDCL “should take all necessary steps to curb the high losses observed in their area of supply.” The commission has provisionally retained the distribution loss targets at 19 percent for KPDCL and 15 percent for JPDCL for the three years of the present control period. The decision is based on the loss-reduction targets already prescribed under successive power-sector reform programmes. The erstwhile Jammu and Kashmir State Electricity Regulatory Commission had fixed a trajectory for reducing Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses to as low as 15 percent by FY 2019-20 under the UDAY scheme. A similar objective was subsequently incorporated under the Ministry of Power's Revamped Reforms-based and Results-linked, Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS). While deciding the Business Plan for FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26, JERC had considered the distribution loss levels submitted by KPDCL and JPDCL on the basis of AT&C loss targets approved by the Ministry of Power under RDSS. The commission noted that the RDSS scheme has now been extended up to March 2028. It also referred to the minutes of the 50th review meeting of RDSS, under which the target for FY 2025-26 under the Result Evaluation Framework would remain the same as the target for FY 2024-25. JERC had earlier approved a distribution loss target of 15 percent for JPDCL and 19 per cent for KPDCL for FY 2025-26. It has now decided that the same targets will provisionally continue for all three years of the present control period. The targets for FY 2027-28 and FY 2028-29, however, will be reviewed in the respective future Annual Revenue Requirement (ARR) orders on the basis of the actual performance of the two distribution companies. The commission's position is particularly important for consumers because distribution losses can arise from both technical and commercial deficiencies in the electricity network. While some losses are inherent in the physical transmission and distribution of electricity, the regulator expects utilities to control losses that can be reduced through better network management, metering, billing, enforcement and other efficiency measures. The commission has therefore drawn a line between legitimate costs of supplying electricity and costs arising from inefficiency. At the same time, the regulator has indicated that higher operating costs cannot automatically be justified by allowing controllable distribution losses to remain high. The commission has also linked the issue to the broader restructuring of the power sector in Jammu and Kashmir. The erstwhile Jammu and Kashmir Power Development Department was restructured and unbundled into separate utilities dealing with generation, transmission and distribution, with the stated objective of making these corporations more self-reliant and cost-efficient. JERC said the restructuring primarily aims at enabling “self-reliant and cost-efficient operation” of the corporations in the generation, transmission and distribution businesses. The commission further observed that financial support and grant-in-aid provided to the utilities during the initial stage of restructuring would need to be gradually phased out. In the future, the revenue requirement for running these utilities is expected to be met through tariffs charged to consumers. The message from the regulator, therefore, is two-fold: consumers will contribute through regulated tariffs towards the legitimate cost of supplying electricity, but KPDCL and JPDCL cannot expect consumers to bear the cost of inefficiencies that remain within the utilities' control.

stories.headline: CM Omar Abdullah lays foundation stone for Fruit & Vegetable Mandi at Tangmarg
stories.title: CM Omar Abdullah lays foundation stone for Fruit & Vegetable Mandi at Tangmarg
stories.summary: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah today laid the foundation stone of a modern Fruit & Vegetable Mandi at Wussan Bangil, Karhama, Tangmarg, marking the beginning of a long-pending demand of the area and a significant step towards strengthening the horticulture marketing infrastructure in the Tangmarg-Gulmarg belt. The proposed mandi will be developed on 50 kanals of land, with direct access to the Tangmarg-Gulmarg Road. Envisaged as a modern and organised marketing facility, the mandi will cater to the major horticulture belt of Tangmarg and adjoining areas and is expected to benefit around nine lakh people across 19 blocks in Baramulla and Budgam districts. The facility will provide growers with an organised platform for the handling, grading, sorting, packaging and marketing of fruit and vegetable produce, besides strengthening market linkages and logistics in the region. It is expected to bring buyers closer to producers, improve price realisation for farmers and reduce post-harvest losses through better handling, storage and supply-chain facilities. Addressing a large public gathering after laying the foundation stone, the Chief Minister said the project represented the fulfilment of a major and long-standing demand of the people of the area and underlined the need to look beyond tourism while assessing the economic potential of Kashmir. “Often, when we speak to people outside J&K, they feel that there is nothing but tourism in Kashmir and that our entire economy revolves around tourism. But when I explain to them that agriculture, horticulture, fruits, dairy and other sectors contribute much more, they are surprised,” he said. The Chief Minister said the establishment of the mandi was particularly important for Tangmarg because the area is a major horticulture-producing belt. “Your fruits and vegetables were being grown here, but to take them to the market you had to travel to far-off markets. You did not always get buyers. Now, through this market, the buyers will come here and, through the buyers, you will get a better rate,” he said. He said the modern infrastructure would also help ensure better quality of produce and facilitate its access to wider markets. The project, he added, would create a new source of income for the area and give a major boost to the rural economy. Emphasising that the success of the mandi would also depend on connectivity, Omar Abdullah directed that the road leading to the facility be improved and widened. “Along with this fruit market and vegetable market, we will have to fix this road as well. Even if it is a 1.5 to 2 km stretch, we will have to widen it and improve its condition so that people do not face any difficulty,” he said. The Chief Minister said the government had initiated development works across sectors in the constituency, including drinking water, healthcare, education, roads and horticulture infrastructure. He said the focus was on taking development works to the ground and addressing the demands of people through concrete projects. The Chief Minister, however, assured the people that the government would make every effort to avoid any further increase during its present term. “I assure you that I will try my best not to increase the electricity tariff during this government,” he said. Chief Minister Omar Abdullah reiterated the government’s commitment to fulfilling the promises made to the people and said the next three and a half years would witness accelerated development across J&K. “God willing, in the next three and a half years, we will fulfil all the promises we have made to the people and present ourselves before you. I say with confidence that after three and a half years, if you look at all the Assembly constituencies, among the most developed, if not the most developed, will be the Gulmarg-Tangmarg constituency, because here not only has work started, it is progressing rapidly,” he said. The Chief Minister also announced that the Mini Secretariat at Tangmarg, whose work had been initiated during his earlier government but could not be completed, would be completed and handed over to the people during the current year. He congratulated the people of Tangmarg, particularly the residents of Wussan, on the foundation stone laying of the Fruit and Vegetable Mandi and said the project would create a stronger and more organised horticulture marketing ecosystem in the area. Earlier, the Chief Minister visited the Kisan Mela showcasing key government initiatives and innovations in agriculture and horticulture. Minister for Agriculture Javid Ahmed Dar and Advisor to the Chief Minister Nasir Aslam Wani spoke on the occasion and highlighted the achievements and initiatives undertaken by the government in agriculture and allied sectors. MLA Gulmarg-Tangmarg Pirzada Farooq Ahmed Shah said that since assuming office, Chief Minister Omar Abdullah had left no stone unturned in accelerating development across Jammu and Kashmir, with particular focus on the Gulmarg-Tangmarg constituency. He said the pace of development under the present government was evident on the ground and alleged that the opposition was unable to accept the reality of ongoing development process. Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) Gurwinder Singh Oberoi, MLA Beerwah Dr Shafi Ahmed Wani, MLA Baramulla Javed Hassan Beigh, MLA Pattan Javed Reyaz Bedar, MLA Uri Dr Sajjad Shafi and MLA Kreeri-Wagoora Irfan Hafiz Lone were present on the occasion. Director, Horticulture, Planning and Marketing, J&K, Ghulam Jeelani Zargar, Director Agriculture Kashmir Sartaj Ahmed Shah, Director Horticulture Kashmir Vikas Anand, besides senior officers of the Agriculture and allied departments, were also present.

MLA Gulmarg-Tangmarg Pirzada Farooq Ahmed Shah said that since assuming office, Chief Minister Omar Abdullah had left no stone unturned in accelerating development across Jammu and Kashmir, with particular focus on the Gulmarg-Tangmarg constituency.
He said the pace of development under the present government was evident on the ground and alleged that the opposition was unable to accept the reality of ongoing development process.

Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) Gurwinder Singh Oberoi, MLA Beerwah Dr Shafi Ahmed Wani, MLA Baramulla Javed Hassan Beigh, MLA Pattan Javed Reyaz Bedar, MLA Uri Dr Sajjad Shafi and MLA Kreeri-Wagoora Irfan Hafiz Lone were present on the occasion.

Director, Horticulture, Planning and Marketing, J&K, Ghulam Jeelani Zargar, Director Agriculture Kashmir Sartaj Ahmed Shah, Director Horticulture Kashmir Vikas Anand, besides senior officers of the Agriculture and allied departments, were also present.

sentences.text: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah today laid the foundation stone of a modern Fruit & Vegetable Mandi at Wussan Bangil, Karhama, Tangmarg, marking the beginning of a long-pending demand of the area and a significant step towards strengthening the horticulture marketing infrastructure in the Tangmarg-Gulmarg belt.

Envisaged as a modern and organised marketing facility, the mandi will cater to the major horticulture belt of Tangmarg and adjoining areas and is expected to benefit around nine lakh people across 19 blocks in Baramulla and Budgam districts.

The Chief Minister also announced that the Mini Secretariat at Tangmarg, whose work had been initiated during his earlier government but could not be completed, would be completed and handed over to the people during the current year.

Chief Minister Omar Abdullah reiterated the government’s commitment to fulfilling the promises made to the people and said the next three and a half years would witness accelerated development across J&K. “God willing, in the next three and a half years, we will fulfil all the promises we have made to the people and present ourselves before you.

stories.headline: Stop burdening teachers with duties beyond teaching: CM Omar Abdullah
stories.title: Stop burdening teachers with duties beyond teaching: CM Omar Abdullah
stories.summary: Srinagar, Aug 25: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday said teachers in Jammu and Kashmir were being burdened with responsibilities far beyond teaching, while the government must do more to address their grievances and provide support needed to perform their duties effectively. Addressing a day-long educational conference organised by the Jammu and Kashmir Teachers Forum (JKTF) at SKICC here, Omar said the future of Jammu and Kashmir rested on its children, but placing the entire responsibility for shaping that future on teachers would be unjust. “If we put all our responsibility on you and say that our teachers will decide what Jammu and Kashmir will be like in the future, then I think there will be a lot of injustice with you, and we will put more pressure on you,” he said. Referring to former President APJ Abdul Kalam’s emphasis on the role of parents and teachers in shaping children, Omar said the teaching profession had become considerably more challenging compared to the past. He recalled a time when students and parents rarely questioned teachers’ authority, saying that in his own childhood he could not remember complaining about a teacher to his parents. Omar cited an anecdote involving his father Dr Farooq Abdullah and his grandfather Sheikh Abdullah to underline the change in attitudes towards teachers. He said when his father was beaten by a teacher during school days and complained to Sheikh Abdullah, the latter instead appreciated the teacher for disciplining his son. “Today, if something happens to the children, parents immediately go to the police station to file an FIR and file a case in the court,” he said. He said that such situations have made it increasingly difficult for teachers to perform their duties. The Chief Minister said teachers were now competing with smartphones, social media, television channels and a host of other distractions to keep students focused. “The new challenge is Artificial Intelligence. How difficult it must be for a teacher to decide whether the child’s assignment is his own creation or the help of artificial intelligence,” he said. Omar also criticised the practice of assigning teachers a wide range of duties not related to classroom teaching. He said teachers were routinely called upon to prepare students for Independence Day and Republic Day functions, International Yoga Day programmes, anti-drug addiction campaigns, besides being deployed for election duties, often at remote polling stations. “When it comes to your problems, unfortunately, your files don’t move forward as fast as the files that we have to put you somewhere else,” he said. CM Omar Abdullah said the government has a responsibility to address teachers’ concerns with the same urgency with which it assigns them official duties. “If you have problems with transfers, DPCs, or vacancies in schools and other things, then we have to solve those problems with the same intensity,” he said. Omar assured the teachers that he and the minister for education, Sakina Itoo, would work to resolve the teachers’ issues. He further highlighted the difficulties faced by teachers posted in remote rural schools, saying that those without influence often remain in village schools while those with connections (influence) manage to secure postings in urban institutions only. He however, expressed concern over dummy admission in government schools, saying that students enrol themselves in government higher secondary schools largely for examination purposes but spend their time at private tuition centres. “There are schools where children take admission only to enter the name and to sit for the board exam. They never come to class. They sit in the tuition centre and spend the whole day there. But we cannot blame teachers for this,” he added. CM Omar Abdullah also acknowledged infrastructure gaps in schools while talking about rented school buildings and unsafe structures being used for students. “It is the responsibility of the government to fix it. We talk about smart classes, but how far have we been able to take smart classes in schools? Smart classes are far away. In some places, we are not able to provide the right structure for schools,” he added. He said that plugging infrastructure gaps was not the responsibility of the teachers but his as the chief minister of J&K. “Filling the vacancies is not your responsibility; it is my job. It is my responsibility to strengthen your hands so that you can do your work properly,” he added. He, however, urged teachers to prepare students to meet the rapidly changing demands of the future and contribute positively to Jammu and Kashmir’s development. Omar also spoke about the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET), saying the issue was linked to laws applicable across the country. “A deadline has been set for this till August 2028, and the government has repeatedly raised its concerns. We will continue to put up the case before the Supreme Court and hope that the issue could be resolved in the interests of teachers and students,” he added. CM Omar Abdullah said that improving the education system required a collective effort and cannot be left to teachers alone. “If we can improve your situation and school infrastructure, then only you will be able to improve the future of your children. But if we fail to deliver and ask you to fix everything, that will not solve the problem,” he added.
